title: Calculating Optical Density Using MCID
author: Andrea Vogel

steps_raw.instruction: If this is the first time, create a folder labeled “Your Name” on the desktop
Open MCiD using the icon on the desktop Stretch the program to cover both screens: the picture should be 1 whole screen
Settings --> Display Format --> Mono (12 bit) --> ok

Settings --> Input Selection --> QICAM – 12 Lightbox Camera --> ok Check that lightbox camera is on (blue and green lights) (switch is on top of camera) Check that color camera (on top of other scope) is also on, because they are daisy-chained together (switch is on top of camera)

steps_raw.title: Adjust magnification and focus
steps_raw.instruction: film is on lightbox for this

steps_raw.title: Adjust magnification and focus
steps_raw.instruction: Digitize button – looks like a video camera Focus using the camera use ink on film to determine if it is in focus If need to adjust magnification, use the crank that the camera arm is attached to has to be on digitize (dialog box open) in order to see it move click ok to take image

steps_raw.title: Establish flat field correction
steps_raw.instruction: remove film for this step

steps_raw.title: Establish flat field correction
steps_raw.instruction: Change pseudocolor (grayscale bar on top menu) to SPECT2VIS

steps_raw.title: Establish flat field correction
steps_raw.instruction: Adjust light intensity using intensity turner on the light box until the blank field of view looks bluish-pink lumens ~1000

steps_raw.title: Establish flat field correction
steps_raw.instruction: Ctrl+click on the Digitize icon --> Flat Field Correction

steps_raw.title: Establish flat field correction
steps_raw.instruction: If there is already a flat field correction established, click “Clear”

steps_raw.title: Establish flat field correction
steps_raw.instruction: Click “Acquire” to establish a new flat field correction Do not change settings!!! (but just in case, they should match the below): Correction source: Digitize Correction method: Pixel by pixel Frame average: 4 Smoothing and Median filters should be clicked Click “ok”

steps_raw.title: Create a Density Calibration
steps_raw.instruction: film is back on the lightbox for this part, looking at the standards slide

steps_raw.title: Create a Density Calibration
steps_raw.instruction: Study type (on left-side menu) --> Standards

steps_raw.title: Create a Density Calibration
steps_raw.instruction: Operations (on left-side menu) --> Calibration ROD – relative optical density
Create a Density Calibration

steps_raw.title: Create a Density Calibration
steps_raw.instruction: Calibrations (on top menu bar) --> Density Change to Cal Stds input lowest to highest values (zero first) Select a density standards file --> ok If you need to create a new calibration table, click “None” Enter numbers from data sheet into “Standards unit” column Data sheet nCi/mg x Decay rate = # entered Click cursor in “Value Read” column next to first standard value Digitize the standards Get a zero reading (from plain film), then procedure through the standards from lightest to darkest

steps_raw.title: Create a Density Calibration
steps_raw.instruction: Select curve type (on dialog box) cubic spline (smoothed) is usually used pick the one that fits the data best (by eye)

steps_raw.title: Create a Density Calibration
steps_raw.instruction: Extrapolate (under curve graph) will tell computer how to interpret data that falls outside the range of the standards “current curve type” for both min and max

steps_raw.title: Sampling
steps_raw.instruction: Operations --> Sample

steps_raw.title: Sampling
steps_raw.instruction: Have laptop nearby with Excel spreadsheet open (don’t use MCiD spreadsheet) example: %s %s

steps_raw.title: Sampling
steps_raw.instruction: change pseudocolor to grayscale

steps_raw.title: Sampling
steps_raw.instruction: Choose whether unilateral or bilateral measuring Usually use unilateral

steps_raw.title: Sampling
steps_raw.instruction: Choose whether free-hand or use shape (rectangle or oval) For VP, use oval useful: ctrl + drag = changes size alt + drag = rotates ctrl + click shape on menu = get measurements (to keep consistent across days/accidental changes) F4 clears image, not data

steps_raw.title: Sampling
steps_raw.instruction: Click on region of interest and background (2 clicks) to get data if you want, hit F4 to clear the image, then re-click to make sure you are getting close numbers Numbers in red are extrapolated from the standards

steps_raw.title: Sampling
steps_raw.instruction: Input data into excel spreadsheet

steps_raw.title: Sampling
steps_raw.instruction: Move to next slice and repeat process

steps_raw.title: Sampling
steps_raw.instruction: When completely done with that animal, clear all the data using “Clear” on sheet

steps_raw.title: Shut down
steps_raw.instruction: turn off camera on the microscope and cover the scope

steps_raw.title: Shut down
steps_raw.instruction: turn off camera on the lightbox

steps_raw.title: Shut down
steps_raw.instruction: put lens cover on the camera

steps_raw.title: Shut down
steps_raw.instruction: wipe down the light box with sparkle and kimwipes

steps_raw.title: Shut down
steps_raw.instruction: place blue lab bench sheet on the light box, soft side down

steps_raw.title: Shut down
steps_raw.instruction: Shut down computer

steps_raw.title: 10.	At end of experiment
steps_raw.instruction: get images

steps_raw.title: 10.	At end of experiment
steps_raw.instruction: use micrometer to determine sizes
